title: Reconciliation
cashByCurrencyHint: What this portfolio's ledger says, one currency at a time. Nothing is converted, so a statement can be compared against it directly.
noCashYet: No cash movement recorded in any currency yet.
compareHint: Paste what your broker reports. Running this twice produces the same result and changes nothing either time.
positionsHint: A difference does not mean these records are wrong. It means two records disagree.
cashHint: Each currency is compared against its own balance. A dollar balance is never weighed against a baht one.
neverRun: No reconciliation has been run yet
neverRunHint: Paste a statement above to compare it against this portfolio. It records what it finds and changes nothing.
transferHint: A transfer re-parents the transactions. Nothing is sold, so no profit or loss is created.
splitsHint: The one corporate action that changes a share count with no transaction behind it. Recording it here restates the history without rewriting a single trade.

form.hint: This compares and records what it finds. It changes no transaction, holding or balance.

findings.nothingCompared: This run compared nothing in this section.
findings.marked: Marked as reviewed. Nothing was changed.

adjustments.effectiveDateHint: The first day trading at the new price. Trades on or after it are already adjusted.
adjustments.notRewritten: Your transactions are not rewritten. Removing this later restores every figure exactly.
adjustments.recorded: Split recorded. Your transactions were not changed.
adjustments.removed: Split removed. Every figure is back to what it was.

transferForm.needsSecond: A transfer needs a second portfolio to move into.
transferForm.needsReason: A transfer needs a reason, so the audit trail explains itself.

correction.title: Correct this transaction
correction.hint: The previous values are kept. Nothing is overwritten without a record of what it was.
correction.historyFailed: The history could not be loaded. The correction above still works.
correction.corrected: Corrected. The original values are kept in the audit trail.
